businessProfile.productSummary: DTC consumer wellness offering (supplements / functional beverages / self-care services) aimed at helping customers 'feel better.'

assumptions: The business sells consumer-facing wellness products or services (not B2B).
The product mix is tangible consumer goods and/or bookingable wellness services (supplements, functional drinks, classes, recovery) rather than purely clinical care or software.
Target customer skews adult wellness consumers (25–45), willing to pay a mid-tier price or subscribe.
The brand wants an outcomes-focused, evidence-friendly message rather than playful novelty.
clarifyingQuestions: What exactly do you sell (choose one): physical wellness products (supplements, drinks), services (classes, therapy, spa), or a mix?
Who is your primary customer (age, gender, geography) and typical order value or price points?
Do you make clinical or health claims that require substantiation, or is messaging focused on mood/feel-good positioning?
Is the business primarily subscription-driven or one-time purchases?

excludedPublishers.reason: Swiftcart is instant convenience/grocery with low AOV ($28) and impulse late-night shoppers—poor fit for mid-tier, evidence-focused wellness DTC where buyers research claims.

Marlowe & Co. serves older affluent women (45–65) with workwear—audience and category (apparel) don't align with a general wellness product unless it's premium classic lifestyle goods, which is not specified.
Linden Park targets 50–70 affluent women for classic apparel; demographic and category mismatch for a mid-market wellness DTC brand aimed at younger wellness buyers.
Everbody is plus-size women's apparel focusing on fit and representation—category mismatch for wellness products unless explicitly targeted clothing-for-comfort, which is not stated.
Pawline is pet-focused (pet food/supplies); its audience shops for pet health, not human wellness products.
Ruffco's massive pet audience is dedicated to pet purchases (pet_food, pet_pharmacy) and unlikely to convert for human wellness goods.
Heartfoot sells basics/gifting (socks/underwear) with gifting-season spikes—category and purchase intent don't align with wellness DTC.
Velvetline is beauty-focused (skincare/makeup) with a Gen Z audience; unless the product is clean-beauty or skincare-focused, it's a weak match for general wellness claims.
Hearthstone Goods sells high-end cookware and targets new-home/gifting—audience purchases kitchen goods, not core wellness consumables.
Kitchenly is meal-kits for families—good for food convenience but not a primary channel for evidence-based wellness supplements or services.
Stride & Stem sells women's shoes (sustainable) to professional women—category mismatch unless product is footwear-for-comfort, which is not described.
Cloudfoot is apparel (shoes/activewear) focused on comfort and sustainability—only marginally relevant unless product ties directly to active recovery or apparel-based comfort.
Tailcrate is pet subscription/ toys—audience buys pet items and is unlikely to be an efficient channel for human wellness goods.
Strandlab focuses on personalized haircare/DTC; unless the advertiser's product is hair/wellness related, audience expects personalization-specific offers rather than general wellness.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Wellness Optimizer actively buys supplements, clean-beauty, and evidence-backed products; age and low price sensitivity match the ranked wellness publishers (Daily Form, Pantrygood).
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Clinically informed solutions that measurably improve how you feel—ingredient transparency and outcomes you can track.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Fitness Enthusiast purchases performance and recovery products and crosses into wellness categories; Movewell and Studiogrid audiences overlap with this persona.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Performance-backed recovery or wellness support that helps you recover faster and feel better for your next workout.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Convenience-First Millennial values subscriptions and speed—if the brand offers convenient replenishment (subscriptions), Kitchenly-adjacent channels and Pantrygood/Pop & Sip audiences will convert.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Easy, subscription-ready wellness—one-click reorder and fast delivery so you feel better without thinking about it.

selectedPersonas.whyRelevant: The Sustainability Buyer responds to specific sustainability claims and clean ingredients; Pantrygood and Northbed audiences care about supply-chain and product safety, which fits if the brand emphasizes transparent sourcing.
selectedPersonas.keyMessage: Sustainably sourced, transparently made wellness products that make you feel better without costing the planet.

variants.headline: Trackable, transparent supplements to help you feel better
variants.body: View full ingredient lists and exact dosages, plus guided pairings for sleep, mood, and recovery—so you can track real changes over weeks. Science-forward formulations and clear labels to support measurable improvements, not gimmicks.
variants.rationale: Focuses on ingredient transparency, measurable outcomes, and integration with tracking—matching an optimizer who pays premiums for evidence-backed, trackable solutions.

variants.headline: Recovery-focused formulas to get you back stronger
variants.body: Targeted recovery and energy support designed for consistent trainers—formulations to help reduce post-workout fatigue and restore what your body needs between sessions. Use pre/post routines to recover faster and stay performance-ready.
variants.rationale: Speaks directly to training and recovery needs with performance-forward language that appeals to athletes who buy products to enhance workouts and results.

variants.headline: One-click wellness: subscribe, receive, feel better—no hassle
variants.body: Subscribe in one click, get fast delivery, and pause or skip anytime. Automatic replenishment of supplements and functional beverages so you feel better without thinking about it—simple checkout, dependable delivery.
variants.rationale: Emphasizes speed, frictionless one-click subscription, and flexible delivery—exactly what a convenience-first millennial values.

variants.headline: Sustainably sourced wellness with full supply-chain transparency
variants.body: Ingredients traced to responsible suppliers, minimal recyclable packaging, and supply-chain details on every product page. Choose wellness that helps you feel better while reducing environmental impact—clear, specific sustainability you can verify.
variants.rationale: Calls out supply-chain traceability, minimal packaging, and on-page details to satisfy a skeptical sustainability buyer who demands specifics over vague eco messaging.

bidStrategy.rationale: Mid-AOV product: pay per click at 1-2% of order value, a sustainable CPC if roughly 1 in 30 clicks converts

budget.rationale: $1500/publisher/month floor for statistically useful volume × 5 publishers × 1 mid-tier multiplier
